subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason why there is a time difference between Mauritius and South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for an explanation (1 + 1):
• The countries are located on two different time zones.
• Mauritius is on UTC +4 time zone and South Africa is on UTC +2 time zone.
• There is a time difference between countries situated on different time zones.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate what time it was in Mauritius when the Dubes arrived in South Africa at 12:00 on 30 April 2020. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: South Africa is UTC +2; Mauritius is UTC +4 (identification of time zones)
Mark 2: Time difference = 4 − 2 = 2 hours; Mauritius is ahead, so add 2 hours to SA time → 12:00 + 2 hours
Mark 3: Time in Mauritius = 14:00

Final answer: 14:00 (full 3 marks awarded for correct final answer with calculations shown)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the departure time of the repatriation flight from Mauritius. Show ALL calculations. (Arrival time in Johannesburg: 12:00; Flying time: 4 hours 30 min)
subQuestions.memoText:
Method 1:
Mark 1: South Africa +2; Mauritius +4; Time difference = 2 hours
Mark 2: Time in Mauritius when SA = 12:00 → 12:00 + 2 = 14:00
Mark 3: Departure time in Mauritius = 14:00 − 4 hours 30 min
Mark 4: Departure time = 09:30

Method 2:
Mark 1: Time difference = 2 hours
Mark 2: Departure (SA time) = 12:00 − 4h30 = 07:30
Mark 3: Convert to Mauritius time: 07:30 + 2 hours
Mark 4: Departure time in Mauritius = 09:30

Final answer: 09:30

subQuestions.questionText: Do you think the Dubes will suffer from jet lag when they land in South Africa? Give ONE reason for your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks (1 for answer + 1 for reason):

subQuestions.questionText: Estelle, a friend from London, stayed in the Dubes' home while they were on holiday in Mauritius. Estelle also had to return to London on a special flight. She departed at 19:00 on 24 April 2020 from the OR Tambo International Airport to London. The flying time was 11 hours. The United Kingdom practises DST during this period. Calculate the date and time when Estelle arrived in London. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Method 1:
Mark 1: London = UTC 0; South Africa = UTC +2
Mark 2: DST applies in London → +1 (i.e. London is on UTC +1 during DST)
Mark 3: Time difference between SA (+2) and London (+1 with DST) = 1 hour (SA is 1 hour ahead)
Mark 4: Convert SA departure to London time: 19:00 − 1 = 18:00
Mark 5: Add flying time: 18:00 + 11 hours
Mark 6: 18:00 + 11 hours = 05:00 (next day)
Mark 7: Arrival time = 05:00 on 25 April 2020

Method 2 (also acceptable):
Mark 1: London 0; SA +2; time difference = 2 hours
Mark 2: Convert SA departure to London standard time: 19:00 − 2 = 17:00
Mark 3: Add flying time: 17:00 + 11 = 04:00 (next day)
Mark 4: Apply DST: +1 hour
Mark 5: Arrival = 05:00
Mark 6: Date = 25 April 2020
Mark 7: Final answer correctly stated

Final answer: 05:00 on 25 April 2020

subQuestions.questionText: Passengers were transferred directly from the aircraft into minibuses. The minibuses took them to the passport control point and then to the baggage collection point. These are not the normal operating procedures at an airport. Give ONE reason why it was necessary to transport the passengers in this way.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for one well-explained reason (1 + 1):
• Contact with other people: so that the South African passengers did not come into contact with any other people at the airport.
• Time constraints: passengers had to get to their quarantine hotel as quickly as possible.
• Social distancing: they were transported in different minibuses.
• Avoiding contamination: passengers had to use the same sanitised minibus throughout the process to avoid contamination.
• Due to the risk of spreading COVID-19.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain THREE ways in which the repatriation process ensured the health and safety of the South African passengers.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-explained way (3 x 2 = 6 marks):
• Contact with other people: contact at airports was limited to avoid the risk of spreading the COVID-19 virus.
• Quarantine: passengers were placed in isolation for the required period after entering South Africa to ensure they were not COVID-19 positive.
• Control for tracking and tracing: passengers were handled as a group on one flight, transported together within and from the airport, and accommodated together in a hotel in Pretoria to make tracking and tracing easier.
• The inbound flight was handled with the strictest health and safety protocols to ensure the South Africans did not compromise their own safety and that of others.

subQuestions.questionText: When the Dubes returned to South Africa, they were left with USD 62,70. Calculate the amount the Dubes would have received when they exchanged the USD for rand. (Use BBR for US dollar = 17,33; round to TWO decimal places.)

Mark 3: Final answer: ZAR 1 086,59

The site shown in photo C represents a mixed heritage site (combines cultural and natural significance).

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why World Heritage Site D has historical significance.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-stated reason (2 x 2 = 4 marks). Site D is Robben Island:
• The facility was used as a prison for political prisoners of South Africa's apartheid regime.
• The buildings represent freedom and the victory of democracy over oppression.
• The island represents resilience and triumph over hardship and adversity.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why the owner of the restaurant requested the manager to cover his arms. (Refer to 'The Contiki Restaurant' scenario in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE correct reason (1 + 1):
• The new manager has tattoos / marks on his arms which do not contribute to a professional image of the business.
• The new manager needs to wear a more formal dress code.
• The new dress code suits his position at work.

subQuestions.questionText: Do you think the owner's request is fair? Give TWO reasons for your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the position taken plus 2 marks for the reasoning. Justified responses are required. Accept either YES or NO with valid reasoning.

YES (with reasons):
• He is the owner and has the right to make the rules.
• He must ensure customer satisfaction and profitability of the business.
• He must ensure that the appearance of the employees does not scare customers away.

NO (with reasons):
• He should have been informed about the dress code prior to the start of his new job.
• He has not set an example in adhering to a dress code.
• The owner could be showing prejudice and discrimination towards tattoos.

Note: Accept examples. Justified responses are required (2 x 2 = 4 marks).

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways in which the manager could have reacted negatively to the owner's request.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each negative reaction stated (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
• The manager could have rejected the request based on freedom of choice.
• The manager could have lodged a complaint of unfair labour practices against the owner with the CCMA / the Human Rights Commission.
• The manager could have defended himself.
• The manager could have verbally abused the owner.

Note: Accept dialogue responses expressing these reactions.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify TWO role players who would benefit from the GCET. (Refer to the UNWTO Global Code of Ethics for Tourism extract in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for each correctly identified role player (2 x 1 = 2 marks). Any TWO of:
• Governments
• The tourism industry
• Communities
• Tourists

subQuestions.label: 8.1.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the pillar of the triple bottom line represented by Article 3 (Tourism, a factor of sustainable development).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for correct pillar:
• Environmental pillar
• Planet

subQuestions.label: 8.1.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the pillar of the triple bottom line represented by Article 5 (Tourism, a beneficial activity for host countries and communities).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for correct pillar:
• Social pillar
• People

subQuestions.questionText: Explain THREE ways in which Article 5 will prevent exploitation (taking advantage) of communities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-explained way (3 x 2 = 6 marks):
• It will ensure tourists behave responsibly when visiting communities.
• It will ensure tourists pay fair prices for local produce and services.
• It will ensure the community perceive tourism as a contributor to economic development in the region.
• The cultures and religion of the local communities will be respected and protected.
• They will learn to protect the environment.
• Policies are put in place and applied.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the business concept driven by King III in the picture above. (Refer to 'Sustainable Tourism Business Practices' extract and picture of the staff of Patels Travel establishing a community food garden.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE correct business concept:
• Corporate Social Investment / Corporate Social Responsibility (CSI / CSR)
• The social pillar of the Triple Bottom Line
• Sustainable tourism practices
• Team building
• Triple Bottom Line approach
• Ethical business practice

subQuestions.questionText: State THREE outcomes this initiative aims to achieve within the community.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each correctly stated outcome (3 x 2 = 6 marks):
• Promotes sustainable development.
• Serves to uplift the community.
• Provides opportunities for local communities.

Note: Accept examples of CSI/CSR initiatives.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the unforeseen global occurrences A, B and C in January 2020. (Refer to the cartoon of global events in January 2020 in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each correct identification (3 x 2 = 6 marks):
• A: Wildfires / Natural disaster / Animals were killed in the fire (e.g. Australian bushfires)
• B: The outbreak of the Corona Virus / Disease / Pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic
• C: Aircraft was shot down / Air disaster / Crash / Missile attack on an aircraft

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss ONE way in which unforeseen global occurrence B impacted on the global tourism industry after March 2020.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for one well-discussed way (1 + 1):
• Due to the Lockdown in certain countries, people were unable to travel.
• Local and international airports in certain countries were closed.
• Certain sectors of the tourism industry shut down.
• Many employees in the tourism and hospitality industries lost their jobs.
• Tourists were left stranded in another country and could not return home.

subQuestions.questionText: From the information above, explain how the outbreak of Covid-19 impacted on the status of international flights. (Refer to the Departure Information at Dubai International Airport in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the explanation (1 + 1):
• Cancellation or delays in all flights — the departure board shows multiple international flights either cancelled or delayed as a direct result of the outbreak.

subQuestions.label: 9.2.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why the flights above were Cancelled.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE correct reason (1 + 1):
• Most countries had closed their borders; airlines were not permitted to land nor was entry of any passengers permitted.
• Countries went into Lockdown due to the COVID-19 pandemic and there was no movement of people.

subQuestions.label: 9.2.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why the flights above were Delayed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE correct reason (1 + 1):
• Some airlines would have had to wait for the necessary authorisation and verification for take-off and landing rights.
• Long queues at the check-in counters due to new screening and safety regulations.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss THREE ways in which the cancellation of flights affected the airline industry.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-discussed way (3 x 2 = 6 marks):
• Some airlines had to shut down due to loss of income and profits from flight cancellations.
• Some airlines had to rely on business rescue packages from their governments or private investors to keep them afloat after mass cancellations of flights.
• Some airlines resorted to retrenchment packages / flight crew members lost their jobs.
• Some airlines restructured their business operations as cost-saving measures.
• Flights were grounded due to lockdown regulations resulting in a loss of income to the employees.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the foreign market that has shown a positive growth in 2019. (Refer to the South Africa's Foreign Tourist Arrivals in 2019 table in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for correct answer:
• Netherlands (2 marks) — the only market in the table showing positive growth (+0,8% up from 2018).

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph, recommend THREE ways in which SATourism, despite the negative perception (thinking) caused by Covid-19, can increase the foreign tourist arrivals to South Africa. NOTE: Your paragraph should focus on changing negative perceptions of Covid-19 and the measures taken by South Africa to safeguard tourists against infection.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-recommended way (3 x 2 = 6 marks). Response must be in paragraph form:
• South Africa needs to reassure foreign tourists that the COVID-19 is on the decrease.
• Gateways into the country, tourist attractions and tourism businesses adhere to the safety protocols that are in place to ensure continuity of a COVID-19 free environment.
• SATourism can structure their marketing initiatives focusing on the success rate of the nation in overcoming the virus.
• Encourage international tourism businesses with a South African link and branches to offer incentive packages for travel to South Africa.
• South Africa can publicise their successes in overcoming the disease in the key foreign source markets.
• Enforcing adherence to COVID-19 protocols according to regulations for both South African and international tourists.

Note: Accept options outlined in learner paragraph responses.

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE web-based customer feedback method.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE correct method:
• Feedback using electronic devices
• Social media platforms (e.g. Facebook, Twitter, Instagram)
• Internet (e.g. online surveys, website feedback forms, email)
• Cell phone (e.g. WhatsApp feedback, SMS)

Note: Accept examples of web-based methods.
